rounds.text: Aarti Drugs Ltd is trading at an attractive valuation relative to its sector, with a P/E ratio of 18.5x and an EV/EBITDA of 13.59x compared to sector benchmarks of 30.8x and 16.42x respectively [E1, E6, E11]. Operational momentum is accelerating significantly, demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 15%, a profit growth of 16%, and a quarterly operating margin expanding to 16% in September 2026 from 13% a year prior [E17, E21, E31]. Cash generation remains robust, backed by a strong cash conversion ratio of 1.30x and an operating cash flow of Rs 254 Cr in March 2026, alongside a healthy domestic institutional accumulation where holdings rose from 5.26% to 10.24% [E34, E35, E43]. Furthermore, technical strength is evident as the stock trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 82 [E50, E51]. Conceded: promoter holding has declined to 54.07% from 57.47%, and the 5-year and 3-year compounded sales growth figures show historical stagnation [E15, E16, E41].

The current market price of ₹ 466 is severely disconnected from fundamental value, sitting at a massive deficit to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 277 per share, which implies a negative margin of safety of 68.0% [E2, E45, E46]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an unrealistic 7.2% growth rate compared to the 0.0% assumed in the base case, leaving the stock vulnerable to any operational misstep [E47]. Long-term top-line expansion has stalled significantly, demonstrated by a dismal 3-year compounded sales growth of -2% and a sluggish 5-year rate of 4% [E15, E16]. Compounded profit growth over the past 5 years has actually contracted by 7%, while the 5-year share price growth stands at -4%, highlighting structural underperformance [E19, E23]. Adding to investor concerns, promoter holdings have steadily eroded from 57.47% in December 2023 to 54.07% in September 2026, accompanied by rising borrowings that climbed to Rs 620 Cr [E39, E41]. Finally, the business is flagged for questionable financial practices, specifically potential capitalization of interest costs, alongside a weak 3-year return on equity of 13.3% and a low dividend payout of just 6.72% [E62, E63, E64]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth has rebounded to 15% alongside positive institutional money flow [E17, E44].

While the bear relies on a DCF model assuming 0% growth to claim overvaluation [E46, E47, E70], the company is currently delivering a significant turnaround with TTM profit growth of 16% and a recent quarterly net profit surge of 84% YoY [E21, E68, E69]. This momentum suggests the stock is under-appreciated, as its P/E of 21.67x and EV/EBITDA of 13.59x trade at substantial discounts to sector benchmarks of 30.8x and 16.42x, respectively [E6, E11]. Although the bear critiques historical ROE and sales [E15, E16, E62], the current ROE of 12.58% and ROA of 6.79% both exceed sector averages [E8, E9], while recent quarterly sales growth of 26% YoY indicates a sharp reversal of past trends [E66, E67]. Conceded: promoter holdings have decreased [E41], borrowings have risen to Rs 620 Cr [E39], and dividend payouts remain low [E64]. However, domestic institutions have nearly doubled their stake to 10.24% [E43], and concerns regarding interest capitalization or profit quality are mitigated by a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.30x, with profits fully backed by Rs 254 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35, E63]. Finally, the bear’s focus on long-term price underperformance [E23] ignores that the company is now outperforming expectations with a relative-strength rating of 82 and a price trend currently above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50, E51, E57].

Conceded: TTM profit growth is 16%, quarterly net profit surged 84% YoY, and quarterly sales grew 26% YoY [E21, E66, E68]. However, leaning on these short-term bursts ignores a poor multi-year track record of 5-year sales growth at 4%, 3-year sales contraction at -2%, and a 5-year profit drop of -7% [E15, E16, E19, E61]. While the bull highlights discounts to sector valuation benchmarks [E6, E11], a rigorous discount cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 277 against a market price of Rs 466, resulting in a severe -68.0% margin of safety [E45, E46, E70]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased their stake and operating cash flow reached Rs 254 Cr [E35, E43], but borrowings also climbed to Rs 620 Cr, promoter holdings declined to 54.07%, and the company was flagged for potentially capitalizing interest costs alongside low dividend payouts [E39, E41, E63, E64]. Finally, pointing to a relative strength of 82 and moving averages [E50, E51] dismisses a dismal 12-month price return of -7.6%, a multi-year share price stagnation, and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -94.6% [E23, E24, E25, E52, E53].
